inputs.original_text: The danger isn’t only whether immigration agents actually show up at polling places; refusing to rule it out can itself frighten people away from voting. Dismissing that fear as something Democrats are “afraid of” ignores how state power falls hardest on communities already exposed to intimidation. With the Trump administration giving inconsistent answers, voters’ rights can’t depend on officials’ assurances. Democracy means little if people have to risk their safety to participate.
inputs.modified_text: The threat doesn’t have to be carried out to suppress participation: uncertainty itself can make people fear that voting puts them at risk. That burden falls especially hard on communities already targeted by state power, and calling their concern partisan only deepens the intimidation. Officials’ inconsistent assurances are no substitute for enforceable protections. A democracy that leaves people to weigh their safety against their right to vote is failing them.
